inspectionNotes: Inspected every required native render and preview. The background-sheet and four-view-sheet are byte-identical, verified by SHA-256, so their common pixels were inspected once. Inspected the standalone at native size and logical 192-by-448 on light, gray and dark backgrounds; inspected repetition and both entrance joins in native and logical previews and raw images. Independently generated temporary nearest-neighbor RGB/alpha seam strips from the hash-verified raw native and sprite assemblies for enlarged inspection. Did not alter candidate files or entrance dependencies.
observations: The native redesign materially improves the original flat wall: canopy tiles now have curved sections, softened thickness and visible edge responses; a coherent chamfered molding frames the wall field; paired capital/support blocks provide a deliberate eave detail; and the low wood base has a readable recessed panel.

These additions survive at logical size as clear architectural forms. They improve the wall's design without filling the background with small decorations or making it compete with the entrance. Original blankness and part counts were not treated as constraints.

Blue canopy, ochre field and honey wood remain distinct. The softer blue highlights and warm timber bevels give the asset more volume than the original. The quieter field remains a useful material and compositional rest area rather than a black or muddy dead spot.

Illumination is balanced across corresponding left/right trim and supports. Broad highlights describe canopy and wood geometry without glaring white streaks, global horizontal shading ramps or directional ground shadows.

Three-wall repetition is coherent in both connected geometry and independent native PNG assembly. Molding and lower-panel repetition reads as deliberate bays; it does not create double-width border posts or exposed terminal caps. The horizontal canopy, fascia and baseboard bands continue across module boundaries.

Both wall-to-entrance connections preserve continuous field color and band heights. The wall canopy's more curved interior forms transition to the unchanged entrance canopy as a controlled modeling difference; the protected end planes and canopy cadence remain aligned.

No material alpha gap, halo, isolated fragment, clipping, black overlap patch or broken corner is visible in the required standalone and connection evidence. Native versus independently assembled differences are confined largely to small edge/shading responses and sampling; neither assembly shows a visible structural or color seam at intended size.
remainingDifferences: The fixed concept has a more bulbous/scalloped canopy, cream accent, brighter golden plaster, larger decorative supports and a taller ornamented base. The native candidate adapts these ideas to the fixed original envelope, protected band heights and approved family palette rather than copying them literally.

The wall field and wood remain smoother and less textured than the concept's plaster flecks and grain. This quieter finish is accepted because the structural details remain readable, material separation is clear and the result fits the frozen entrance family.
The concept's target fringe, loose alpha pixels and different canvas padding are intentionally absent.

Across canopy y175:405, fascia y460:495, field y650:1080 and baseboard y1168:1235, every sampled seam alpha is 255. Mean absolute adjacent RGB jumps range from approximately 0.37 to 1.67 code values; the maximum is 7. Enlarged RGB/alpha strips show no material join defect.
technicalEvidence.nativeVersusSprite: Across 4,857,063 mutually opaque joined-context pixels, 99 percent have maximum per-pixel channel difference at most 6; the maximum is 48 at native coordinate (1245,410), near a canopy edge response. Only 4,361 pixels exceed 16. Directly inspected raw/context and join images show no material mismatch at logical size.
